summary: Accordion, from the 'Component --- Accordion' sheet. Compound: Item, Trigger, Panel, with plain and card variants and a panel whose height animates. Unusually, the DESIGN was drawn against the behaviour layer's anatomy -- the sheet's layers are named Accordion Root / Item / Header / Trigger / Panel / Panel Inner Container, which are Base UI's parts exactly -- so the DOM here is that structure one-for-one and every value on the sheet has a single place to land. Trigger renders the Header AND the button as one part, because the header carries nothing of its own; both data-slots are present so the DOM still matches the sheet layer for layer. WHY NOT <details>/<summary>, since the platform does a real share of this: summary is not a button and its ARIA mapping is inconsistent across screen readers, while the sheet's row is a heading CONTAINING a control; the panel height has to animate, and the behaviour layer publishes --accordion-panel-height where the native route needs ::details-content plus interpolate-size (one engine today); single/multiple has to be driven from state, where `name` is markup-level; and hiddenUntilFound exists for find-in-page. NOT one of the reasons, though it was the first one written down: arrow-key navigation between headers does NOT exist -- `loopFocus` is accepted as a prop and no key handler is implemented, confirmed in the source and then in the browser. Arrow keys are OPTIONAL in the APG accordion pattern so Tab-only conforms; the claim was removed and the actual behaviour is pinned by a test rather than left to be rediscovered as a bug. Three things the behaviour layer does that a wrapper must not assume away, each found by testing rather than by reading: `multiple` defaults to false (which is what the sheet draws); a disabled trigger is marked aria-disabled and KEPT FOCUSABLE rather than given the native attribute, so `disabled:` and `enabled:` variants match nothing and both shipped here as dead classes until the test caught them; and the chevron's rotation has to hang off the TRIGGER's data-panel-open through a group variant, since a child never has that attribute itself. headingLevel is a prop with no guessed default, for the same reason Card's is. onValueChange is re-wrapped so the behaviour layer's second event-details argument never reaches a consumer's signature.

migration.manual: New item, nothing to migrate. Two notes for anyone extending it. `@base-ui/react/accordion` was added to optimizeDeps.include in apps/storybook/vitest.config.ts -- the list must grow with every new behaviour-layer subpath or the first run after adding a story flakes. And do not reach for `disabled:`/`enabled:` variants on the trigger: the behaviour layer uses aria-disabled and keeps the control focusable, so style it with aria-disabled variants.
